title: Burgh Island Hotel: Agatha Christie & Poirot Guide, Devon
description: Burgh Island Hotel, an Art Deco tidal island hotel in Devon, inspired Agatha Christie and starred in Poirot's Evil Under the Sun.
h1: Burgh Island Hotel: Agatha Christie's Art Deco island
intro: Off the Devon coast, an Art Deco hotel sits on a tidal island that you reach on foot at low tide or by sea tractor at high tide. Agatha Christie knew it well.
filming: The 2001 Poirot TV adaptation of Evil Under the Sun used the island as a filming location, and several scenes from the BBC's 1987 Miss Marple adaptation Nemesis were filmed in the hotel. Christie's novels Evil Under the Sun and And Then There Were None are both said to have been inspired by the island.
facts: The Art Deco hotel was completed in 1929 for the film-maker Archibald Nettlefold, and Wikipedia credits the architect as Matthew Dawson.
Nettlefold bought the island in 1927; a small monastery had existed there around the 1330s.
The hotel has 25 rooms, one built from the captain's cabin of HMS Ganges (1821).
The building is Grade II listed.
The hotel's Beach House was reportedly built for Agatha Christie, who had her home at Greenway nearby.
visit: Check the tide timetable before travelling. Evening dress codes and Art Deco dinners are part of the experience.
